finding.claim: The DELETE handler calls the async authorize() without await, so the authorization check never gates the delete. Any user can delete any report. When authorize() rejects with a 403, nothing handles the rejection, and it becomes an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the Node process (Node 15+ default).
finding.source: Any authenticated request (or any request where req.session.user exists) to DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary report id. The caller has no grant on that report.
finding.sink: db.reports.remove(report.id) at server.js:21, the destructive operation that should be protected by the 'delete' grant.

trace.note: DELETE /reports/:id handler; id comes from req.params.id
report is loaded by attacker-supplied id; there is no ownership or tenant scoping
authorize(...) returns a Promise that is not awaited, so execution continues before the grant check finishes and any thrown 403 is not caught by the handler
authorize() is async. Its db.grants lookup and its throw happen asynchronously, so the failure cannot stop the handler
db.reports.remove runs unconditionally, then 204 is returned

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is authorize(), which is not awaited. The PUT handler at line 27 does await it, which confirms the intended behaviour. No other middleware performs authorization. The global middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user and does not enforce authentication or check for a missing session.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 on missing grant, but the DELETE handler at line 20 calls it without await, so the check does not gate line 21. The global middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user and enforces nothing. No other guard exists.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls the async authorize() as a bare statement with no await, so the rejection from line 14 cannot stop db.reports.remove at line 21, and any session user can delete any report (the PUT handler at line 27 does await it). The unhandled rejection can also crash Node 15+.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 is async and throws 403 on a missing grant, but the DELETE handler calls it without await (line 20), so the throw never gates line 21. The global middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user. PUT at line 27 awaits it correctly.
verdict_facts.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() as a bare statement without await, so the 403 thrown at server.js:14 cannot stop db.reports.remove at server.js:21, and any user who reaches the route can delete any report.

finding.claim: Mass assignment: the PUT handler passes the entire req.body to db.reports.update. A user with only the 'write' grant can overwrite any field of the report, such as owner_id, id, or ACL and tenant fields, if the db layer does not whitelist fields. This is plausible but depends on the unseen db implementation.
finding.source: JSON body of PUT /reports/:id, fully attacker-controlled through express.json().

trace.note: express.json() parses an arbitrary JSON object into req.body
authorize checks the 'write' grant only, with no field-level control
req.body is passed unfiltered to the update call

finding.guards_checked: There is no schema validation or field allowlist in this file. The db implementation is not present, so whether it filters fields is unverified. Authorization at line 27 is correctly awaited.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 when the 'write' grant is missing, and the PUT handler awaits it at line 27, so it works as a guard. There is no field allowlist or schema validation in this file. db is not defined or imported anywhere, and server.js is the only file in the directory.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches, and the attacker needs only the 'write' grant (server.js:27). But server.js:28 passes req.body unfiltered to db.reports.update, and whether that function whitelists fields cannot be determined because the db implementation is absent.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:27 (awaited, throws 403 without 'write' grant); no field allowlist or schema validation in this file; db layer not present.
verdict_facts.reason: The trace is accurate (server.js:3 express.json, :27 awaited authorize, :28 passes raw req.body to db.reports.update), but whether the db layer filters fields like owner_id or id is not visible, so exploitability cannot be decided from this directory.
